You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From ce9f30105f06712c67be3c5c8dd814182d2b8b44 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2012 16:53:46 +0400
Subject: [PATCH] Fix SAS base32 codec

This fixes issues introduced in commit b2e073c422729ed7807ffcc42012df38ba4b7b78

Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>
---
 c_src/sas_nif.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/c_src/sas_nif.c b/c_src/sas_nif.c
index d804590..f9e9e23 100644
--- a/c_src/sas_nif.c
+++ b/c_src/sas_nif.c
@@ -566,7 +566,7 @@ static int b32(ErlNifEnv* env, int argc, const ERL_NIF_TERM argv[])
 	bytes[0] = ((uint8_t*)(bin.data))[0];
 	bytes[1] = ((uint8_t*)(bin.data))[1];
 	bytes[2] = ((uint8_t*)(bin.data))[2] & 0xf0;
-	bits = (bytes[0]  << 24) | (bytes[1] << 16) | (bytes[0] << 0) | 0;
+	bits = (bytes[0]  << 24) | (bytes[1] << 16) | (bytes[2] << 8) | 0;
 
 	for (i=0,shift=27; i!=4; ++i,shift-=5){
 		n = (bits>>shift) & 31;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect bitwise operation in the base32 encoding function, specifically in the way the `bits` variable was being constructed. The original code mistakenly used `bytes[0]` twice instead of using `bytes[2]` for the third byte, leading to incorrect data being processed and potentially resulting in invalid base32 encoded output. The fix correctly shifts `bytes[2]` into the appropriate position, ensuring that the encoding logic functions as intended.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect bitwise operation in the base32 encoding function, specifically in the way the `bits` variable was being constructed. The original code mistakenly used `bytes[0]` twice instead of using `bytes[2]` for the third byte, leading to incorrect data being processed and potentially resulting in invalid base32 encoded output. The fix correctly shifts `bytes[2]` into the appropriate position, ensuring that the encoding logic functions as intended.
